title: Ringed pro-etale open extension preserves products and Roos triangles
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $R_U=j^{-1}R$, and use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $J=D(j_!)$ for termwise exact ringed extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For every countable family $C_n\in D(R_U)$, the canonical morphism $J(\prod_n C_n)\to\prod_n JC_n$ is an isomorphism, whose $n$th projection is $J$ of the original projection. For every inverse system $(C_n,d_n)$ and every distinguished Roos triangle $C\xrightarrow{c}\prod_n C_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n C_n\to C[1]$ [def-weil-inverse-system] [def-weil-derived-limit], applying $J$ and these canonical product isomorphisms gives a distinguished Roos triangle $JC\to\prod_n JC_n\xrightarrow{1-s_J}\prod_n JC_n\to (JC)[1]$ for the transitions $Jd_n$. Its first map has components $J(c_n)$, where $c_n$ is the $n$th component of $c$. No constructibility, boundedness or constant-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For module sheaves $M_n$ on $U$, apply the existing ringed sheaf-product theorem to the small family indexed by $\mathbf N$. It gives the natural isomorphism $\phi_M:j_!(\prod_nM_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nj_!M_n$ whose $n$th component is $j_!(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. Its hypotheses hold for the present quasi-compact open immersion and arbitrary ring sheaf $R$, with restricted ring $R_U=j^{-1}R$. In particular it requires neither that $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated nor that $R$ be constant. Naturality in maps of families will allow this comparison to be used degreewise in complexes.

source.place: Tag 09BP (lemma-j-shriek-limits); ringed refinement already stated in lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products

proof.text: Choose complexes $A_n$ representing $C_n$. Apply the preceding comparison in every degree. Its naturality with respect to differentials makes $j_!(\prod_nA_n)\to\prod_nj_!A_n$ an isomorphism of complexes, with precisely the termwise image projections. By the derived-product theorem for arbitrary ring sheaves on the pro-etale site, these termwise products represent the products in both unbounded derived categories, with their specified projections. Exactness of $j_!$ gives its termwise triangulated derived functor $J$. Localizing the complex comparison therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $\Phi:J(\prod_nC_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nJC_n$, characterized by $q_n\Phi=J(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. This characterization also makes it independent of the representing complexes.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), combined with det-pe-products-derived and the preceding sheaf comparison

proof.text: Put $P_C=\prod_nC_n$, $P_J=\prod_nJC_n$, $t=1-s$ and $t_J=1-s_J$. For each projection $q_n:P_J\to JC_n$, additivity and functoriality of $J$ give $q_n\Phi J(t)=J(\mathrm{pr}_nt)=J(\mathrm{pr}_n-d_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=J(\mathrm{pr}_n)-J(d_n)J(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=(q_n-J(d_n)q_{n+1})\Phi=q_nt_J\Phi$. Uniqueness in the product universal property implies $\Phi J(t)=t_J\Phi$. Likewise $q_n\Phi J(c)=J(\mathrm{pr}_nc)=J(c_n)$. These equations apply to arbitrary derived transition maps; no simultaneous strict tower representative is required.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit): coordinate description of the transition endomorphism

proof.text: Apply the triangulated functor $J$ to the given distinguished triangle. Identify its two middle objects with $P_J$ by $\Phi$ and its fourth object with $(JC)[1]$ by the shift comparison $\xi:J(C[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(JC)[1]$. The resulting triangle has first arrow $\Phi J(c)$, middle arrow $t_J$ by the preceding calculation, and last arrow $\xi J(\delta)\Phi^{-1}$, where $\delta:P_C\to C[1]$ is the original last arrow. It is isomorphic as a triangle to the image triangle and hence distinguished by TR1. It is the required Roos triangle by the definition of a derived limit, and its first arrow has components $J(c_n)$ as computed above.
